bib.title: MiniGPT-4: Enhancing Vision-Language Understanding with Advanced Large Language Models

question: Does aligning a frozen visual encoder with a frozen advanced LLM (Vicuna) through one projection layer reproduce GPT-4-style vision-language abilities?
hypothesis: GPT-4's multimodal abilities stem from using a more advanced LLM; aligning visual features properly with such an LLM yields them.
contributions: Aligning visual features with Vicuna gives advanced vision-language abilities comparable to GPT-4 demos
Training only one projection layer suffices, about 10 hours on 4 A100
Short caption pairs alone give unnatural output; a small detailed-description set in stage 2 fixes it

method.summary: MiniGPT-4 connects BLIP-2's EVA-CLIP ViT-G/14 and Q-Former to Vicuna via one linear layer; only that layer trains. Stage 1 trains on about 5M caption pairs; stage 2 finetunes on 3,500 self-generated, ChatGPT-repaired, hand-checked detailed descriptions in a conversational template.

datasets.name: Curated detailed descriptions
datasets.source: 5,000 random Conceptual Captions images, described by the stage-1 model, repaired by ChatGPT, filtered by hard-coded rules and manually
datasets.preprocessing: Generation continued with '###Human: Continue ###Assistant:' if output under 80 tokens

datasets.name: COCO captions
datasets.size: 5000 images (Table 2); 100 test images for failure counts
datasets.preprocessing: one random ground-truth caption as reference

models.name: MiniGPT-4
models.architecture: frozen vision stack + one linear projection + frozen Vicuna

other.trainable: one linear projection layer; count not stated

training.objective: Linear-layer output used as soft prompt; LLM generates ground-truth text; no regression loss on the image-prompt part in stage 2
training.wall_clock: stage 1 about 10 hours; stage 2 about 7 minutes

other.stage2_template: ###Human: ###Assistant:, instruction sampled from a predefined set

metrics.name: Human success count
metrics.definition: Evaluators judge whether generation satisfies the request

metrics.name: COCO coverage correctness
metrics.definition: ChatGPT answers yes/no whether generated caption covers all objects and relations of one reference caption

metrics.name: Failure rate
metrics.definition: Manually counted failed generations out of 100

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests stated; human judges for Table 1 (number and instructions not stated), ChatGPT judge for Table 2, manual counts for Table 3.

prompts.purpose: Generate detailed descriptions for stage-2 data
prompts.text: ###Human: Describe this image in detail. Give as many details as possible. Say everything you see. ###Assistant:

Fix the error in the given paragraph. Remove any repeating sentences, meaningless characters, not English sentences, and so on. Remove unnecessary repetition. Rewrite any incomplete sentences. Return directly the results without explanation. Return directly the input paragraph if it is already correct without explanation.

There is one image caption1 '{ground-truth caption}', and there is another image caption2 '{comparison caption}'. Does image caption2 cover all the objects and visual relations shown in image caption1? Only answer yes or no without any explanation.

results.claim: Stage-2 finetuning cuts failed detailed-caption generations from 35% to 2% (manual count).
results.setup: 100 random COCO test images, prompt 'Describe the image in detail.', MiniGPT-4 before vs after stage 2; failures counted by hand
results.table: Table 3, row After stage-2, column Detailed caption

results.claim: Stage-2 finetuning cuts failed poem generations from 32% to 1%.
results.setup: 100 random COCO test images, prompt 'Can you write a beautiful poem about this image?'; manual count
results.table: Table 3, row After stage-2, column Poem

results.claim: MiniGPT-4 satisfies 65 of 100 advanced-task requests vs 5 of 100 for BLIP-2.
results.setup: Own 100-image set, 25 per task (meme, recipe, ad, poem); human evaluators judge whether the generation satisfies the request
results.quote: MiniGPT-4 shows strong performance and successfully responses to 65% of the requests.

results.claim: MiniGPT-4 explains only 8 of 25 memes correctly (BLIP-2: 0/25).
results.setup: Same 100-image human-judged set, prompt 'Explain why this meme is funny.'

results.claim: COCO caption coverage judged by ChatGPT: MiniGPT-4 66.2% vs BLIP-2 27.5%.
results.metric: correctness (ChatGPT yes/no coverage of reference caption)
results.setup: 5000 COCO images, one random ground-truth caption as reference, ChatGPT judge
results.note: Table 2 gives 3310/5000 vs 1376/5000; the 5000 denominator appears only in the table
results.quote: With a success rate of 66.2%, MiniGPT-4 is considerably more accurate than BLIP-2, which achieves only 27.5%.

results.claim: Stage 1 trains in about 10 hours on 4 A100 80GB.
results.setup: 20,000 steps, batch 256, about 5M image-text pairs, only the linear layer trained
results.quote: Our model undergoes 20,000 training steps with a batch size of 256, covering approximately 5 million image-text pairs. The entire process takes about 10 hours to complete, utilizing 4 A100 (80GB) GPUs.

results.claim: Stage 2 takes 400 steps at batch 12, around 7 minutes on one A100.
results.quote: only requiring a mere 400 training steps with a batch size of 12, which takes around 7 minutes with a single A100 GPU

results.claim: About 3,500 of 5,000 generated descriptions survive ChatGPT repair, rule filtering and manual checking.
results.setup: 5,000 random Conceptual Captions images described by the stage-1 model
results.quote: only approximately 3,500 out of 5,000 image-text pairs satisfy our requirement

results.claim: Without the Q-Former, AOK-VQA is 56.9 and GQA 33.4, similar to the full model (58.2 / 32.2).
results.setup: Ablation, variant trained the same way
results.table: Table 4, row (a) MiniGPT-4 w/o Q-Former, columns AOK-VQA, GQA

results.claim: Three linear layers instead of one lowers AOK-VQA to 49.7 (GQA 31.0).
results.table: Table 4, row (b) MiniGPT-4 + 3 Layers, column AOK-VQA

results.claim: Also finetuning the Q-Former gives AOK-VQA 52.1, GQA 28.0.
results.table: Table 4, row (c) MiniGPT-4 + Finetune Q-Former, column AOK-VQA

results.claim: Longer captions hallucinate more: CHAIRi 9.6 at 175 words vs 7.2 at 28.8 words; BLIP-2 1.3 at 6.5 words.
results.setup: MiniGPT-4 (long) prompt 'Please describe this image as detailed as possible.'; unit of CHAIRi not printed
results.note: CHAIRi unit not printed; Table 5 also lists average length 175, 28.8, 6.5 words

results.claim: On traditional VQA, original MiniGPT-4 trails BLIP-2 (58.2 vs 80.2 AOK-VQA; 32.2 vs 42.4 GQA); unfreezing Vicuna with LoRA plus VQA data gives 67.2 / 43.5.
results.setup: BLIP-2 trained on 129M pairs, MiniGPT-4 on 5M; the Finetune Vicuna variant adds LoRA and VQAv2, OKVQA, A-OKVQA data in stage 2
results.note: The Finetune Vicuna variant is an ablation, not the released MiniGPT-4

limits: Hallucination in detailed descriptions is unresolved (CHAIRi rises with caption length)
Lags BLIP-2 on traditional VQA; main evidence is qualitative and a 100-image hand-judged set
Optimizer, learning rate, schedule, precision, Vicuna size and trainable parameter count not stated
The claim that GPT-4's abilities come from an advanced LLM is not tested directly; BLIP-2 FT comparison also changes the LLM and training recipe

lineage.note: Reuses its ViT-G/14 and Q-Former; main baseline
Used in the A.2 unfrozen-Vicuna ablation
